newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bel-20 changes take share volume to 1990s high.
newsitem.headline: Bel-20 changes take share volume to 1990s high.

text.p: Fireworks flashed on the Brussels bourse on Friday as a reshuffle of share weights in the Bel-20 index .BFX of leading stocks propelled volumes to levels not seen before this decade.

The Brussels bourse said total volume in Belgian shares was 8.97 billion Belgian francs, while volume in Bel-20 stocks was about 8.5 billion francs. Kredietbank, the main beneficiary of the reshuffling, chalked up 1.07 billion francs.
"The bangs and flashes were there, especially in the last hour of trade," said a dealer, when index funds in particular made the last adjustments to their portfolios.

The all-time record -- 18.77 billion francs -- was set on the February 8, 1988 during the battle for control of holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA between Italian financier Carlo de Benedetti and Cie de Suez.
As a comparison, average daily volume on the bourse in July, before the traditionally quieter August month, had been 2.7 billion Belgian francs.
Looking ahead, traders were split on whether there would be more fallout from the changes to the index next week or whether players had now adapted their holdings to the new weights.
"We could see a consolidation, or a bit of a correction, on Monday," said a dealer. On the other hand, there might be support from the continuing fall in long-term interest rates.
Another predicted the effect of the changes to the index would wear on as some players had been waiting for the index-linked action to be over before returning.
"Some shares are overvalued," he added, citing Societe Generale de Belgique. The stock eased five francs to 2,525. At levels just below 2,600 francs the share was too expensive.
Sentiment turned against SGB after its recent bid for a large Tractebel stake, he noted.
"SGB has not got the cash for it," he added. The 49 billion franc purchase of a 25 percent stake was announced on Tuesday.

The day's main gainer was Solvay, up 110 francs at 19,300. The chemical share rose on news of a capital gain of some six billion francs from the sale of its animal health businesses to American Home Products Corp.

Solvay also said at a news conference on the sale it would spend the proceeds on acquiring human pharmaceutical product lines or companies in the U.S. Solvay reiterated it hoped 1996 current earnings would be in line with those of 1995.
Dealers said the share benefitted from the twin effects of the good news and a larger weight in the Bel-20.
